questions.question_text: In SQL, what is a correlated subquery?

A subquery that is independent of the outer query
A subquery that joins two tables
A subquery that returns multiple rows

Complete the following query to rank employees based on their salaries within each department:

FROM Employees;

GROUP BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC

correct_answer: It forces SQL Server to recompile the query each time it is executed, potentially improving performance for parameter-sensitive queries.

It allows for faster updates and deletions.
It eliminates the need for additional indexes on the table.

It forces SQL Server to use the index for all queries.

A process to backup the database
A method to join multiple tables together
A command to rollback a transaction
correct_answer: A situation where two or more transactions are waiting for each other to release locks, causing them to be stuck

questions.question_text: Which of the following can help prevent deadlocks?
choices: Ensuring transactions acquire locks in the same order
Reducing the size of the database
correct_answer: Ensuring transactions acquire locks in the same order

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to explicitly lock a row or table in SQL Server?
What is the purpose of the SAVEPOINT command in SQL?
choices: To set a point within a transaction to which you can later roll back
To create an index on a table
correct_answer: To set a point within a transaction to which you can later roll back

questions.question_text: Which isolation level ensures that once a row is read by a transaction, it cannot be changed by other transactions until the first transaction is complete?
Which isolation level prevents other transactions from inserting or updating rows that would qualify for a query until the transaction is complete?
What is the difference between a COMMIT and a ROLLBACK statement?
choices: COMMIT saves all changes made in a transaction, while ROLLBACK undoes all changes
COMMIT starts a new transaction, while ROLLBACK ends it
COMMIT locks the database, while ROLLBACK unlocks it
COMMIT creates a backup, while ROLLBACK restores it
correct_answer: COMMIT saves all changes made in a transaction, while ROLLBACK undoes all changes

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential consequence of using the READ UNCOMMITTED isolation level?
choices: Dirty reads, where a transaction reads data that has not yet been committed
Deadlocks, where transactions are stuck waiting for each other
Increased database size due to additional locking
correct_answer: Dirty reads, where a transaction reads data that has not yet been committed

questions.question_text: What is a phantom read in SQL Server?
choices: A situation where a transaction re-reads data and finds rows that were not there previously
A method to rollback a transaction
A command to backup the database
correct_answer: A situation where a transaction re-reads data and finds rows that were not there previously

questions.question_text: Which isolation level can prevent phantom reads?
What is the purpose of the XLOCK hint in SQL Server?
choices: To take an exclusive lock on a table or row, preventing other transactions from accessing it
correct_answer: To take an exclusive lock on a table or row, preventing other transactions from accessing it

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to view the current locks held by active transactions?
What is the main benefit of using the SNAPSHOT isolation level?
choices: It provides a consistent view of the data without locking, reducing contention between transactions
It ensures that no data is ever lost
It speeds up the retrieval of rows from a table
correct_answer: It provides a consistent view of the data without locking, reducing contention between transactions

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential drawback of using the SERIALIZABLE isolation level?
choices: It can lead to decreased concurrency and increased locking, potentially slowing down the system
It prevents the creation of indexes
correct_answer: It can lead to decreased concurrency and increased locking, potentially slowing down the system

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the NOLOCK hint in SQL Server?
choices: To allow a query to read data without acquiring locks, potentially increasing performance but risking dirty reads
To lock a row or table exclusively
correct_answer: To allow a query to read data without acquiring locks, potentially increasing performance but risking dirty reads

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature automatically detects and resolves deadlocks by choosing one transaction as a victim?
What is the purpose of the TRANSACTION log in SQL Server?
choices: To record all changes made to the database, allowing recovery in case of failure
correct_answer: To record all changes made to the database, allowing recovery in case of failure

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to end a transaction and permanently save all changes?
Which of the following is a key feature of the SERIALIZABLE isolation level?
choices: It prevents other transactions from reading or writing to the data until the transaction is complete
It reduces locking and increases concurrency
correct_answer: It prevents other transactions from reading or writing to the data until the transaction is complete

questions.question_text: What does the SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL statement do in SQL Server?
choices: It sets the isolation level for the current session, determining how transactions interact with each other
It creates an index on a table
correct_answer: It sets the isolation level for the current session, determining how transactions interact with each other

questions.question_text: Which SQL statement is used to manually end a transaction and discard all changes made?
What is the primary purpose of SQL Server authentication?
choices: To verify the identity of users trying to connect to the SQL Server
To manage permissions for database objects
To encrypt data stored in the database
correct_answer: To verify the identity of users trying to connect to the SQL Server

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of SQL Server Windows Authentication?
choices: It uses Active Directory to authenticate users
It requires a separate username and password for SQL Server
It is less secure than SQL Server Authentication
It does not support encrypted connections
correct_answer: It uses Active Directory to authenticate users

questions.question_text: What is the role of a SQL Server login?
choices: To provide access to SQL Server at the instance level
To manage user permissions within a specific database
correct_answer: To provide access to SQL Server at the instance level

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to manage user permissions on database objects?
What is a SQL Server role?
choices: A collection of permissions that can be assigned to users
A database schema used to organize objects
A set of tables and views used to store data
A process that automatically backs up databases
correct_answer: A collection of permissions that can be assigned to users

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of using roles in SQL Server?
choices: They simplify the management of user permissions
They reduce the need for database backups
correct_answer: They simplify the management of user permissions

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the GRANT statement in SQL Server?
choices: To assign permissions to users or roles
To remove permissions from users or roles
correct_answer: To assign permissions to users or roles

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to encrypt data at rest?
What is the purpose of SQL Server auditing?
choices: To track and log activities and changes within the database
To manage user roles and permissions
correct_answer: To track and log activities and changes within the database

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature provides encryption for specific columns within a database?
What is the role of a SQL Server certificate?
choices: To support encryption of data at rest and in transit
correct_answer: To support encryption of data at rest and in transit

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a security best practice for SQL Server?
choices: Using SQL Server Authentication for all users
Allowing unrestricted access to all users

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server roles?
choices: To manage user permissions and access to database objects
correct_answer: To manage user permissions and access to database objects

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of SQL Server encryption?
choices: It protects sensitive data from unauthorized access
It reduces the size of the database
correct_answer: It protects sensitive data from unauthorized access

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a function of SQL Server's Row-Level Security?
choices: It restricts access to rows in a database table based on the characteristics of the user executing a query
It encrypts data at rest in the database
It tracks and logs database activities
correct_answer: It restricts access to rows in a database table based on the characteristics of the user executing a query

questions.question_text: What does the SQL Server REVOKE statement do?
choices: It removes previously granted permissions from a user or role
It grants new permissions to a user or role
It creates a new database role
correct_answer: It removes previously granted permissions from a user or role

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Data Masking feature?
choices: To obfuscate sensitive data by displaying masked values instead of actual data to unauthorized users
To encrypt data in the database
correct_answer: To obfuscate sensitive data by displaying masked values instead of actual data to unauthorized users

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to limit the visibility of specific rows to specific users?
What is the purpose of SQL Server's Logins?
choices: To control access to SQL Server at the instance level
To manage permissions within a database
correct_answer: To control access to SQL Server at the instance level

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common use of SQL Server's Schema permissions?
choices: To manage access to groups of database objects within a schema
To encrypt data in the database
correct_answer: To manage access to groups of database objects within a schema

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows for encryption of data both at rest and in transit?
What is the main advantage of SQL Server's Always Encrypted feature?
choices: It ensures that sensitive data is always encrypted both in storage and in use, even during query processing.
It automatically compresses data to save space.
It allows SQL Server to execute queries faster.
It improves the readability of complex queries.
correct_answer: It ensures that sensitive data is always encrypted both in storage and in use, even during query processing.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)?
choices: To encrypt an entire database to protect data at rest
To encrypt individual columns within a database
To create encrypted backups of the database
correct_answer: To encrypt an entire database to protect data at rest

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a security best practice when creating SQL Server logins?
choices: Use complex passwords that include a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
Use simple passwords to make them easy to remember.
Reuse the same password across all logins.
correct_answer: Use complex passwords that include a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

questions.question_text: What is the role of SQL Server's Database Users?
choices: To define permissions within a specific database
To control access to SQL Server at the instance level
To encrypt data within the database
correct_answer: To define permissions within a specific database

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows for defining and enforcing policies across multiple SQL Server instances?
Which of the following is a feature of SQL Server's Audit Logs?
choices: They capture and store information about events that occur in the SQL Server instance, such as changes to data or permissions.
They automatically create backups of the database.
correct_answer: They capture and store information about events that occur in the SQL Server instance, such as changes to data or permissions.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Security Principals?
choices: To represent entities that can request SQL Server resources, such as logins, users, and roles.
To encrypt data within the database.
To create and manage database triggers.
correct_answer: To represent entities that can request SQL Server resources, such as logins, users, and roles.

questions.question_text: What is the benefit of using SQL Server's Always Encrypted feature in a multi-tenant environment?
choices: It ensures that sensitive data remains encrypted and cannot be accessed by unauthorized tenants, even if they share the same database.
It improves the performance of the database.
It allows SQL Server to handle larger volumes of data.
It simplifies the management of user permissions.
correct_answer: It ensures that sensitive data remains encrypted and cannot be accessed by unauthorized tenants, even if they share the same database.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for managing SQL Server permissions?
choices: Use the principle of least privilege, granting users only the permissions they need to perform their tasks.
Grant all users full administrative privileges.
Disable all security features to simplify management.
Reuse the same set of permissions for all users, regardless of their roles.
correct_answer: Use the principle of least privilege, granting users only the permissions they need to perform their tasks.

questions.question_text: What is the role of SQL Server's Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)?
choices: To assign permissions to roles, which can then be assigned to users, simplifying the management of user permissions.
To encrypt data in the database.
To create and manage database triggers.
correct_answer: To assign permissions to roles, which can then be assigned to users, simplifying the management of user permissions.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a database backup?
choices: To create a copy of the database that can be restored in case of data loss
To improve the performance of the database
correct_answer: To create a copy of the database that can be restored in case of data loss

questions.question_text: Which of the following backup types captures only the data that has changed since the last full backup?
What is the main advantage of using a transaction log backup in SQL Server?
choices: It allows for point-in-time recovery by capturing the sequence of transactions.
It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.
It compresses the database to save space.
It improves the performance of queries.
correct_answer: It allows for point-in-time recovery by capturing the sequence of transactions.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to automate the scheduling of backups?
What is the purpose of a copy-only backup?
choices: To create a backup without affecting the sequence of conventional backups.
To create a backup that includes all data and schema changes.
To compress the backup file to save space.
correct_answer: To create a backup without affecting the sequence of conventional backups.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a full database backup?
choices: It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.
It only captures changes made since the last backup.
It compresses the database to save space.
It only captures the transaction log.
correct_answer: It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of log shipping in SQL Server?
choices: To automatically send transaction log backups to a secondary server for disaster recovery.
To compress database logs to save space.
To manage user permissions across multiple databases.
To encrypt data in transit between servers.
correct_answer: To automatically send transaction log backups to a secondary server for disaster recovery.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to restore a database to a specific point in time?
What is the primary purpose of a restore operation in SQL Server?
choices: To recover a database to a previous state in case of data loss or corruption.
To improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: To recover a database to a previous state in case of data loss or corruption.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for database backups?
choices: Store backups in a secure, off-site location.
Store backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
correct_answer: Store backups in a secure, off-site location.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's backup compression feature?
choices: To reduce the size of the backup file, saving storage space.
To improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: To reduce the size of the backup file, saving storage space.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to restore specific pages of a database instead of the entire database?
Which of the following is a benefit of using differential backups?
choices: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the RESTORE VERIFYONLY command in SQL Server?
choices: To verify that a backup can be read and is not corrupted, without actually restoring it.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
To compress the backup file to save space.
correct_answer: To verify that a backup can be read and is not corrupted, without actually restoring it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using backup encryption in SQL Server?
choices: It protects backup data from unauthorized access.
It improves the performance of queries.
It reduces the size of the backup file.
correct_answer: It protects backup data from unauthorized access.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using differential backups in combination with full backups?
choices: They provide faster recovery times by allowing you to restore only the changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: They provide faster recovery times by allowing you to restore only the changes since the last full backup.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for ensuring the reliability of database backups?
choices: Regularly test backups by restoring them to a separate environment.
Store backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
correct_answer: Regularly test backups by restoring them to a separate environment.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's tail-log backup?
choices: To capture any transactions that occurred since the last transaction log backup, ensuring that no data is lost during the restore process.
To compress the backup file to save space.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
correct_answer: To capture any transactions that occurred since the last transaction log backup, ensuring that no data is lost during the restore process.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to create a backup of the transaction log?
Which of the following is a common use case for SQL Server's filegroup backup?
choices: To backup only specific filegroups in a database, reducing the size and time required for the backup.
To backup the entire database, including all data and schema.
To improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: To backup only specific filegroups in a database, reducing the size and time required for the backup.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of SQL Server's backup retention policy?
choices: To define how long backups should be kept before they are deleted, helping to manage storage space.
To improve the performance of backups.
To compress the backup file to save space.
correct_answer: To define how long backups should be kept before they are deleted, helping to manage storage space.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for database recovery planning?
choices: Regularly update and test the recovery plan to ensure it meets current business needs.
Store all backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
correct_answer: Regularly update and test the recovery plan to ensure it meets current business needs.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows for the creation of a backup strategy that includes full, differential, and transaction log backups?
What is the purpose of the SQL Server RESTORE HEADERONLY command?
choices: To return information about the backup, such as the backup start and end time, without actually restoring the data.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
To compress the backup file to save space.
correct_answer: To return information about the backup, such as the backup start and end time, without actually restoring the data.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using SQL Server's backup compression feature?
choices: It reduces the size of the backup file, saving storage space and potentially speeding up the backup process.
It improves the performance of queries.
correct_answer: It reduces the size of the backup file, saving storage space and potentially speeding up the backup process.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using log shipping in SQL Server?
choices: It provides an automated way to maintain a standby server that can take over in case of primary server failure, ensuring high availability.
It improves the performance of queries.
It compresses the database logs to save space.
correct_answer: It provides an automated way to maintain a standby server that can take over in case of primary server failure, ensuring high availability.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's backup encryption feature?
choices: To protect backup data from unauthorized access.
To compress the backup file to save space.
To improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: To protect backup data from unauthorized access.

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows you to automate the backup and recovery process?
What is the benefit of using differential backups in SQL Server?
choices: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
correct_answer: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.

quizzes.quiz_name: Power BI DAX: A to Z Comprehensive and Concise

questions.question_text: What is Power BI primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Power BI is a data visualization tool that allows users to create interactive dashboards and reports.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI is available in Desktop, Service, and Mobile versions.
questions.explanation: Power BI is available as Power BI Desktop (for creating reports), Power BI Service (for sharing and collaborating), and Power BI Mobile (for accessing reports on the go).

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Power BI can connect to various ______ including Excel, SQL Server, and web data sources.
questions.explanation: Power BI supports connections to a wide range of data sources, making it a versatile tool for data analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a component of Power BI?
questions.explanation: Power BI Server is not a component of Power BI. The main components are Power BI Desktop, Gateway, and Service.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI Desktop is used for report creation and data modeling.
questions.explanation: Power BI Desktop is the primary tool used for creating reports and data models in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Power BI Mobile allows users to access their reports on ______.
questions.explanation: Power BI Mobile provides access to reports and dashboards on mobile devices, ensuring data is available on the go.

questions.question_text: Match the following Power BI components with their descriptions.

definitions: Used for creating reports and data models
Used for accessing reports on the go

correct_answer.Power BI Desktop: Used for creating reports and data models
correct_answer.Power BI Mobile: Used for accessing reports on the go

questions.explanation: Understanding the different components of Power BI is crucial for effectively using the tool.

questions.question_text: Explain the role of Power BI Gateway.
questions.explanation: Power BI Gateway is used to connect on-premises data sources to Power BI, enabling cloud-based reports to access on-premises data.

questions.question_text: Which Power BI component is primarily used for real-time dashboards?
questions.explanation: Power BI Service is used for hosting and managing real-time dashboards and reports.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI can only connect to structured data sources.
questions.explanation: Power BI can connect to both structured and unstructured data sources, providing flexibility in data analysis.

questions.question_text: What does DAX stand for?
questions.explanation: DAX stands for Data Analysis Expressions, the formula language used in Power BI, Power Pivot, and SQL Server Analysis Services.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX is only used in Power BI.
questions.explanation: DAX is also used in Power Pivot for Excel and SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS), not just Power BI.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: DAX allows users to create ______ columns and measures in Power BI.
questions.explanation: Calculated columns and measures are created using DAX to perform calculations on data in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key feature of DAX?
questions.explanation: DAX supports iterative calculations, allowing complex operations to be performed on data row by row.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX can perform both row-level and aggregated calculations.
questions.explanation: DAX can perform calculations at both the row level (e.g., using SUMX) and the aggregated level (e.g., using SUM).

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: A DAX ______ is a pre-defined calculation that can be used in a Power BI report.
questions.explanation: A DAX measure is a pre-defined calculation, such as SUM(Sales[Amount]), that can be reused in reports.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their uses.

definitions: Calculates the total of a column
Calculates the mean value of a column

correct_answer.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
correct_answer.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

questions.explanation: These basic DAX functions are used to perform common calculations in Power BI.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a calculated column in Power BI?
questions.explanation: Calculated columns are used to perform calculations at the row level, such as calculating a total for each sale.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX is a case-sensitive language.
questions.explanation: DAX is not case-sensitive; 'SUM' and 'sum' are treated the same.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The ______ function in DAX is used to apply logic, returning different results based on a condition.
questions.explanation: The IF function is used to apply conditional logic in DAX, similar to how it's used in Excel.

questions.question_text: Which of the following DAX formulas correctly calculates the total sales from a 'Sales' table?
questions.explanation: The correct formula is SUM(Sales[Total]), which adds up all the values in the 'Total' column of the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: True or False: The formula SUMX(Sales, Sales[Amount] * Sales[Quantity]) calculates the total revenue by multiplying 'Amount' by 'Quantity' for each row and then summing the results.
questions.explanation: SUMX is an iterator function that processes row by row and calculates 'Sales[Amount] * Sales[Quantity]' for each row before summing the results.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX formula to calculate the average sales amount per transaction is ______.
questions.explanation: AVERAGE(Sales[Amount]) calculates the mean value of the 'Amount' column in the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their uses.

choices.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
choices.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

correct_answer.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
correct_answer.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

questions.explanation: These basic DAX functions are used to perform common calculations in Power BI.

questions.question_text: What is the result of the following DAX formula: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Category] = 'Electronics')?
choices: Total amount of sales for the 'Electronics' category
Number of sales in the 'Electronics' category
correct_answer: Total amount of sales for the 'Electronics' category
questions.explanation: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Category] = 'Electronics') calculates the total sales amount only for rows where the category is 'Electronics'.

questions.question_text: True or False: The following formula returns the first non-blank value in the 'Date' column: FIRSTNONBLANK(Sales[Date], Sales[Amount]).
questions.explanation: FIRSTNONBLANK(Sales[Date], Sales[Amount]) returns the first date where the corresponding 'Amount' is not blank.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To concatenate 'FirstName' and 'LastName' in a 'Customers' table, you would use the formula ______.
questions.explanation: CONCATENATE is used to join two text strings, such as first and last names, into a single string.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their uses.

choices.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
choices.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

correct_answer.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
correct_answer.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

questions.explanation: These basic DAX functions are used to perform common calculations in Power BI.

questions.question_text: How would you use the SWITCH function to return a specific value based on a category? Provide an example.
questions.explanation: SWITCH evaluates 'Sales[Category]' and returns 'Discounted' if it's 'Electronics', 'Standard' if it's 'Furniture', or 'Other' for any other value.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common data source that can be connected to Power BI?
questions.explanation: Power BI can connect to a wide range of data sources, including Excel, JSON, SQL Server, and many more.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power Query is the tool used in Power BI for data transformation.
questions.explanation: Power Query is the ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) tool in Power BI, used for transforming and cleaning data before analysis.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Power Query Editor allows users to ______ data before loading it into the Power BI model.
questions.explanation: Power Query Editor is used to transform data, including filtering, shaping, and merging data from various sources.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tasks can be performed in Power Query Editor?
questions.explanation: Power Query Editor is used to prepare data by merging tables, cleaning data, and performing other transformation tasks before the data is loaded into Power BI.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power Query Editor can be used to perform calculations using DAX.
questions.explanation: Power Query Editor is used for data transformation, while DAX calculations are performed after data is loaded into the Power BI model.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To remove unwanted columns in Power Query Editor, use the ______ option.
questions.explanation: The 'Remove Columns' option in Power Query Editor allows you to exclude unnecessary columns from your data model.

questions.question_text: Match the following data transformation steps with their descriptions in Power Query Editor.

definitions: Combine columns from two tables based on a common key
Stack tables on top of each other
Summarize data by aggregating based on specified fields

correct_answer.Merge Queries: Combine columns from two tables based on a common key
correct_answer.Append Queries: Stack tables on top of each other
correct_answer.Group By: Summarize data by aggregating based on specified fields

questions.explanation: Understanding how to merge, append, and group data in Power Query is essential for preparing data for analysis in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Explain the role of data cleansing in Power BI.
questions.explanation: Data cleansing involves removing errors, duplicates, and inconsistencies from data to prepare it for accurate analysis in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the 'Group By' function in Power Query?
choices: Combining multiple rows into a single row based on specific criteria
Joining tables together based on a common field
Pivoting data from rows to columns
correct_answer: Combining multiple rows into a single row based on specific criteria
questions.explanation: The 'Group By' function aggregates data by combining multiple rows into a single row based on specified criteria, often used for summarization.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power Query Editor automatically detects and suggests data types for each column during the data import process.
questions.explanation: Power Query Editor has an 'Automatic Data Type Detection' feature that suggests data types based on the content of each column during import.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function would you use to create a calculated column for total sales in a 'Sales' table?
questions.explanation: SUMX is used to perform calculations row by row, such as multiplying quantity by unit price to get the total sales.

questions.question_text: True or False: You can create relationships between tables in Power BI using DAX.
questions.explanation: Relationships between tables are created using the Power BI interface, not DAX. DAX is used for calculations and data modeling within those relationships.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To create a calculated measure for total profit, you would use the formula ______.
questions.explanation: SUMX is used here to calculate total profit by subtracting unit cost from unit price for each sale and then summing the results.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function is used to filter a table before performing calculations?
questions.explanation: FILTER is used in DAX to apply filters to a table, enabling calculations on a subset of the data.

questions.question_text: True or False: The RELATED function in DAX can be used to bring in data from a related table.
questions.explanation: The RELATED function retrieves values from a related table, based on existing relationships in the data model.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: In DAX, the ______ function removes all filters from a column or table.
questions.explanation: The ALL function in DAX clears all filters, allowing calculations to consider all data in the specified table or column.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their correct uses.

choices.RELATED: Brings in data from a related table
choices.CALCULATE: Modifies a filter context for a calculation
choices.FILTER: Applies a filter to a table before performing calculations

correct_answer.RELATED: Brings in data from a related table
correct_answer.CALCULATE: Modifies a filter context for a calculation
correct_answer.FILTER: Applies a filter to a table before performing calculations

questions.explanation: These DAX functions are fundamental for performing complex data modeling tasks in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Describe the purpose of creating calculated columns in Power BI.
questions.explanation: Calculated columns allow dynamic row-level calculations, such as computing total sales or profit per transaction.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function can be used to create time intelligence calculations, such as year-to-date or month-to-date totals?
questions.explanation: DATESYTD is used in DAX to calculate year-to-date totals, a common time intelligence calculation in Power BI.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX measures are calculated dynamically as the user interacts with a report.
questions.explanation: DAX measures are dynamic and recalculated whenever a user interacts with the report, such as applying filters or slicing data.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of creating hierarchies in a data model?
choices: To organize data into different levels
correct_answer: To organize data into different levels
questions.explanation: Hierarchies in a data model are used to organize data into different levels, such as Year, Quarter, Month, making it easier to analyze data at varying levels of detail.

questions.question_text: True or False: Row-Level Security (RLS) can be implemented using DAX in Power BI.
questions.explanation: Row-Level Security (RLS) can be implemented in Power BI using DAX expressions to control data access based on user roles.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Time intelligence functions in DAX, such as ______, are used to calculate time-based aggregations like year-to-date or quarter-to-date totals.
questions.explanation: DATESYTD is a common DAX time intelligence function used to calculate year-to-date totals.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function would you use to create a dynamic measure that returns different values based on the user's selection in a report?
questions.explanation: The SWITCH function is used to create dynamic measures that return different values based on a user's selection or condition.

questions.question_text: True or False: Calculated columns are stored in the data model, while DAX measures are calculated on the fly.
questions.explanation: Calculated columns are stored in the data model as part of the table, while DAX measures are calculated dynamically when the report is viewed.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: ______ is a DAX function that can be used to shift dates by a specified number of days, months, or years, often used in time intelligence calculations.
questions.explanation: DATEADD is used in DAX to shift dates by a specified period, making it useful for time-based comparisons like moving averages.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their advanced data modeling uses.

choices.CALCULATE: Modifies a filter context for a calculation
choices.USERELATIONSHIP: Activates an inactive relationship in the data model
choices.RELATEDTABLE: Returns a table related to the current table

correct_answer.CALCULATE: Modifies a filter context for a calculation
correct_answer.USERELATIONSHIP: Activates an inactive relationship in the data model
correct_answer.RELATEDTABLE: Returns a table related to the current table

questions.explanation: These DAX functions are used for advanced data modeling techniques, such as modifying relationships and filter contexts.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of Row-Level Security (RLS) and how it is implemented using DAX.
questions.explanation: Row-Level Security (RLS) in Power BI restricts data access based on the user's role, and it is implemented using DAX expressions that filter data accordingly.

questions.question_text: Which function in DAX can be used to calculate the running total of a measure across a specified period?
questions.explanation: TOTALYTD is used to calculate the running total or year-to-date total for a measure, commonly used in financial reports.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX allows you to create calculated tables that can be used like any other table in your data model.
questions.explanation: Calculated tables are created using DAX expressions and can be used in the same way as regular tables in your data model.

questions.question_text: You have a 'Sales' table. Which of the following DAX formulas correctly calculates the total sales amount?
questions.explanation: The correct formula is SUM(Sales[Amount]), which adds up all the values in the 'Amount' column of the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: Given the DAX formula: SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Price]), what does this formula calculate?
choices: The total sales revenue by multiplying Quantity and Price for each row.
The total of the Quantity column.
correct_answer: The total sales revenue by multiplying Quantity and Price for each row.
questions.explanation: SUMX is an iterator function that evaluates the expression 'Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Price]' for each row and then sums the results.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX formula AVERAGE(Sales[Amount]) calculates the average sales amount.
questions.explanation: AVERAGE(Sales[Amount]) computes the mean value of the 'Amount' column in the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To find the first non-blank value in the 'Date' column of the 'Sales' table, you would use the formula ______.
questions.explanation: The formula FIRSTNONBLANK(Sales[Date], Sales[Amount]) returns the first non-blank date from the 'Date' column, considering only rows where 'Amount' is not blank.

questions.question_text: You need to combine 'FirstName' and 'LastName' into a full name in the 'Customers' table. Which DAX formula would you use?
questions.explanation: The CONCATENATE function is used to join two text strings into one, such as combining first and last names.

questions.question_text: True or False: The formula MAX(Sales[Amount]) returns the highest sales amount from the 'Sales' table.
questions.explanation: MAX(Sales[Amount]) returns the largest value in the 'Amount' column.

questions.question_text: Given the formula COUNTROWS(Sales), what does it calculate?
choices: The total number of rows in the 'Sales' table.
The sum of the sales amount.
The total quantity of items sold.
correct_answer: The total number of rows in the 'Sales' table.
questions.explanation: COUNTROWS(Sales) returns the total number of rows in the 'Sales' table, which is useful for counting records.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their correct purposes in data analysis.

choices.SUM: Calculates the total of a column.
choices.AVERAGEX: Calculates the average of an expression evaluated row by row.
choices.MIN: Returns the smallest value in a column.

correct_answer.SUM: Calculates the total of a column.
correct_answer.AVERAGEX: Calculates the average of an expression evaluated row by row.
correct_answer.MIN: Returns the smallest value in a column.

questions.explanation: Understanding these basic DAX functions helps you perform common data analysis tasks in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Describe how the IF function can be used to create a calculated column that shows 'High' if sales amount is greater than 1000 and 'Low' if it is less or equal.
questions.explanation: The IF function is used to apply conditional logic, returning 'High' when the condition is true and 'Low' otherwise.

questions.question_text: You have a 'Sales' table and need to calculate the average revenue per sale. Which of the following DAX formulas would you use?
questions.explanation: AVERAGEX calculates the average of an expression evaluated for each row, which in this case is the sales amount.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX formula CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Sales[Region])) removes the filter on the 'Region' column before summing the 'Amount' column.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE modifies the filter context and ALL removes any filters applied to the 'Region' column.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To calculate the maximum profit in the 'Sales' table considering discounts, you would use the formula ______.
questions.explanation: MAXX evaluates the expression for each row, here calculating the profit after discount, and then returns the maximum value.

questions.question_text: Given the DAX formula: SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Price]), what result does it return?
choices: The total revenue by multiplying quantity by price for each sale.
The sum of the quantity column.
The average price across all sales.
The total number of sales transactions.
correct_answer: The total revenue by multiplying quantity by price for each sale.
questions.explanation: SUMX calculates the expression 'Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Price]' for each row and then sums the results, giving total revenue.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function DISTINCT returns all unique values from a column, ignoring duplicates.
questions.explanation: DISTINCT returns a one-column table that contains only the unique values from the specified column.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To calculate the median sales amount in the 'Sales' table, you would use the DAX function ______.
questions.explanation: MEDIAN returns the middle value in a sorted list of sales amounts, effectively dividing the dataset in half.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX aggregation functions with their correct descriptions.

choices.SUMX: Sums up an expression evaluated row by row.
choices.AVERAGEX: Calculates the average of an expression evaluated row by row.
choices.COUNTX: Counts the number of rows where an expression is not blank.

correct_answer.SUMX: Sums up an expression evaluated row by row.
correct_answer.AVERAGEX: Calculates the average of an expression evaluated row by row.
correct_answer.COUNTX: Counts the number of rows where an expression is not blank.

questions.explanation: These iterator functions in DAX operate row by row, allowing for complex calculations that are evaluated individually for each row.

questions.question_text: Describe the purpose of using the CALCULATE function with the ALL function in a DAX expression. Provide an example.
questions.explanation: The CALCULATE function modifies the filter context for a calculation, and using ALL inside it removes any filters from the specified columns. For example, CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Sales[Region])) calculates the total sales amount ignoring any region-based filters.

questions.question_text: You need to calculate the year-to-date (YTD) sales for your 'Sales' table. Which of the following DAX formulas would you use?
questions.explanation: TOTALYTD(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Date]) calculates the year-to-date total by summing the 'Amount' column, filtered by the 'Date' column.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function DATESBETWEEN is used to filter dates between two specified dates.
questions.explanation: DATESBETWEEN is a time intelligence function that filters dates in a column that fall between two specified dates.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To calculate the month-to-date (MTD) sales, you would use the formula ______.
questions.explanation: TOTALMTD(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Date]) calculates the month-to-date total by summing the 'Amount' column, filtered by the 'Date' column.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function would you use to calculate the same period last year (SPLY) sales?
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Sales[Date]) returns the corresponding period from the previous year, making it ideal for year-over-year comparisons.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function PREVIOUSYEAR returns the sales amount for the entire previous year.
questions.explanation: PREVIOUSYEAR is a time intelligence function that returns a table containing all the dates in the previous year, but you need to use it within a calculation (e.g., SUM) to get the sales amount.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ shifts dates by a specified number of days, months, or years.
questions.explanation: DATEADD is used in DAX to move dates by a specified number of intervals, such as days, months, or years.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX time intelligence functions with their correct descriptions.

choices.TOTALYTD: Calculates the year-to-date total for a measure.
choices.DATESINPERIOD: Returns a range of dates based on a specified start date and interval.
choices.SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR: Returns the corresponding period in the previous year.

correct_answer.TOTALYTD: Calculates the year-to-date total for a measure.
correct_answer.DATESINPERIOD: Returns a range of dates based on a specified start date and interval.
correct_answer.SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR: Returns the corresponding period in the previous year.

questions.explanation: Understanding these time intelligence functions is essential for performing date-based calculations in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Describe how the DAX function DATESYTD can be used to calculate a running total for the year. Provide an example.
questions.explanation: The DATESYTD function is used to calculate a running total for the current year. For example, CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), DATESYTD(Sales[Date])) calculates the year-to-date sales amount.

questions.question_text: You need to create a calculated measure for a weighted average price in a 'Sales' table. Which DAX formula would you use?
questions.explanation: To calculate a weighted average, you multiply the quantity by the price for each sale and then divide the total by the sum of the quantities.

questions.question_text: True or False: You can use the CALCULATE function to modify the filter context and apply multiple conditions in a DAX expression.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE is one of the most powerful functions in DAX, allowing you to modify the filter context with multiple conditions.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ is used to perform complex calculations by iterating over each row of a table.
questions.explanation: SUMX is an iterator function that evaluates an expression for each row and then sums the results, making it useful for complex row-based calculations.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function would you use to calculate the cumulative total of sales across a specific time period?
questions.explanation: This formula calculates the cumulative total by summing the sales amounts up to the current date within the specified period.

questions.question_text: True or False: The FILTER function in DAX can be used to filter a table based on a complex condition that can't be applied through relationships or standard filters.
questions.explanation: FILTER allows you to create complex conditions and filter tables in ways that aren't possible with standard relationships or filters.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The ______ function in DAX allows you to return different values based on multiple conditions.
questions.explanation: The SWITCH function is used to evaluate an expression and return different results depending on the value of the expression.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their correct purposes in complex calculations.

choices.CALCULATE: Modifies the filter context for complex calculations.
choices.SUMX: Evaluates an expression for each row in a table and then sums the results.
choices.FILTER: Applies a complex filter to a table.
choices.SWITCH: Returns different values based on multiple conditions.

correct_answer.CALCULATE: Modifies the filter context for complex calculations.
correct_answer.SUMX: Evaluates an expression for each row in a table and then sums the results.
correct_answer.FILTER: Applies a complex filter to a table.
correct_answer.SWITCH: Returns different values based on multiple conditions.

questions.explanation: These DAX functions are crucial for performing advanced calculations, allowing for dynamic, context-specific results.

questions.question_text: Describe how the CALCULATE function can be combined with FILTER to perform a running total calculation in a DAX expression. Provide an example.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE modifies the filter context, and when combined with FILTER, it can be used to calculate a running total by summing all sales up to the current date.

questions.question_text: You notice that a DAX query is taking a long time to execute. Which of the following practices can help optimize DAX query performance?
choices: Avoid using complex calculations in calculated columns
Use the EARLIER function whenever possible
Avoid filtering columns with high cardinality
correct_answer: Avoid filtering columns with high cardinality
questions.explanation: High cardinality columns have many unique values, making them expensive to filter. Avoid filtering such columns directly to improve performance.

questions.question_text: True or False: Using variables in DAX can help improve query performance by reducing redundant calculations.
questions.explanation: Variables store the results of expressions and can be reused in DAX queries, reducing redundant calculations and improving performance.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ can be used to reduce the size of a model by summarizing data before aggregating.
questions.explanation: GROUPBY is used to group data and perform aggregations, reducing the size of the data model and improving performance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following DAX functions should be used sparingly due to its potential to slow down performance?
questions.explanation: LOOKUPVALUE is powerful but can be slow, especially when used in large datasets, as it performs row-by-row lookups.

questions.question_text: True or False: Reducing the number of calculated columns in your model can help improve the performance of your DAX queries.
questions.explanation: Calculated columns consume memory and processing power, so reducing their number can improve overall model performance.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To optimize a DAX query, it's recommended to replace calculated columns with ______ whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Measures are calculated on the fly and don't consume storage space, making them more efficient than calculated columns.

questions.question_text: Match the following optimization techniques with their corresponding benefits in DAX queries.
questions.explanation: These optimization techniques are essential for improving the efficiency and performance of your DAX queries.

questions.question_text: Describe how using variables in a DAX query can improve performance, and provide an example of when this would be beneficial.
questions.explanation: Using variables in DAX can store intermediate results and prevent the need for redundant calculations. For example, storing the sum of sales in a variable can be reused in multiple calculations, reducing processing time.

questions.question_text: You need to calculate the sales rank of each product within its category. Which DAX pattern would you use?
questions.explanation: This pattern uses RANKX along with FILTER and EARLIER to calculate the rank of a product within its category based on sales amount.

questions.question_text: True or False: The 'Dynamic Segmentation' DAX pattern allows you to group data dynamically based on user-defined thresholds.
questions.explanation: Dynamic Segmentation is a powerful DAX pattern that lets you group data based on dynamic criteria set by the user, such as sales ranges.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The ______ DAX pattern is used to calculate the moving average over a specified period.
questions.explanation: The Moving Average pattern smooths out fluctuations in data by calculating the average over a defined rolling window.

questions.question_text: Which DAX function is commonly used in the 'Parent-Child Hierarchies' pattern to traverse a hierarchy and calculate cumulative values?
questions.explanation: The PATH function is used to navigate through parent-child hierarchies, helping to calculate cumulative values or traverse hierarchical paths.

questions.question_text: True or False: The 'Basket Analysis' DAX pattern is used to identify the most common combinations of items purchased together.
questions.explanation: Basket Analysis is a DAX pattern used in retail analytics to find common combinations of items that are frequently purchased together.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The ______ DAX pattern is used to compare a value against the same period in the previous year, adjusted for changes in the number of days.
questions.explanation: Year-over-Year (YoY) Growth is a pattern that compares values from one year to the same period in the previous year, adjusted for differences in the number of days.

questions.question_text: Match the following advanced DAX patterns with their correct descriptions.

choices.RANKX with FILTER: Calculates rank within a subset of data
choices.Moving Average: Smooths data by averaging over a rolling period
choices.Dynamic Segmentation: Groups data based on dynamic thresholds

correct_answer.RANKX with FILTER: Calculates rank within a subset of data
correct_answer.Moving Average: Smooths data by averaging over a rolling period
correct_answer.Dynamic Segmentation: Groups data based on dynamic thresholds

questions.explanation: These advanced DAX patterns are essential for performing complex data analysis and creating dynamic, context-sensitive calculations.

questions.question_text: Describe the 'Dynamic Segmentation' DAX pattern and provide an example of how it can be used to group sales data into performance tiers (e.g., High, Medium, Low).
questions.explanation: Dynamic Segmentation allows you to group data based on user-defined criteria, such as creating performance tiers (High, Medium, Low) by comparing sales amounts against thresholds.

questions.question_text: You need to calculate the Gross Profit Margin for your company. Which of the following DAX formulas would you use?
questions.explanation: Gross Profit Margin is calculated as (Revenue - Cost) / Revenue, which shows the percentage of revenue that exceeds the cost.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function DIVIDE is preferred over the division operator (/) for financial calculations because it handles division by zero more gracefully.
questions.explanation: DIVIDE is preferred because it can return a specific result or blank when dividing by zero, avoiding errors in financial calculations.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To calculate the Year-over-Year (YoY) growth in revenue, you would use the DAX function ______.
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is used to compare revenue or other measures against the same period in the previous year.

questions.question_text: Which of the following DAX patterns is used to analyze financial ratios, such as Return on Investment (ROI)?
questions.explanation: This pattern calculates ROI by dividing the profit from an investment by the cost of the investment, using CALCULATE to filter the relevant data.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX can be used to perform variance analysis, comparing actual performance against budgeted amounts.
questions.explanation: DAX is powerful for financial analysis, including variance analysis, where actual results are compared to budgeted or forecasted amounts.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ can be used to calculate cumulative totals, which are important in financial statement analysis.
questions.explanation: TOTALYTD calculates the cumulative total of a measure, such as revenue or profit, over a specified period.

questions.question_text: Match the following financial DAX patterns with their descriptions.

choices.Gross Profit Margin: Calculates the percentage of revenue that exceeds the cost.
choices.ROI: Measures the profitability of an investment relative to its cost.
choices.YoY Growth: Compares performance against the same period in the previous year.

correct_answer.Gross Profit Margin: Calculates the percentage of revenue that exceeds the cost.
correct_answer.ROI: Measures the profitability of an investment relative to its cost.
correct_answer.YoY Growth: Compares performance against the same period in the previous year.

questions.explanation: These financial analysis patterns are essential for evaluating a company's performance using DAX.

questions.question_text: Describe how the DAX function SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR can be used in financial analysis to calculate Year-over-Year growth, and provide an example.
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is used to compare the performance of a measure, such as revenue, against the same period in the previous year. For example, CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Revenue]), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Sales[Date])) calculates the revenue for the same period last year.

lessons.lesson_name: 5.2 DAX for Sales and Marketing Analytics

questions.question_text: You want to segment your customers into different categories based on their total purchase amount. Which DAX function would you use?
questions.explanation: The IF function can be used to segment customers based on their purchase amount, categorizing them as 'High' or 'Low' spenders.

questions.question_text: True or False: The RANKX function in DAX can be used to rank customers based on their total purchases.
questions.explanation: RANKX is used to rank customers or other entities based on a specific measure, such as total purchase amount, allowing you to identify top customers.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ can be used to calculate the average purchase amount per customer.
questions.explanation: AVERAGEX is used to calculate the average of an expression evaluated over a table, such as the average purchase amount per customer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following DAX formulas would you use to calculate the percentage of total sales contributed by each product?
questions.explanation: This formula divides the sales amount for each product by the total sales amount across all products, using CALCULATE and ALL to remove filters.

questions.question_text: True or False: The CROSSJOIN function in DAX can be used to analyze combinations of products purchased together.
questions.explanation: CROSSJOIN returns the Cartesian product of two tables, allowing you to analyze combinations of items purchased together, which is useful in basket analysis.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To calculate the customer lifetime value (CLV), you would typically use the DAX function ______.
questions.explanation: SUMX is often used to calculate CLV by summing the value of a customer’s purchases over time, adjusted for discounts or returns.

questions.question_text: Match the following sales and marketing DAX patterns with their applications.

choices.RANKX: Ranks customers or products based on a measure.
choices.CROSSJOIN: Analyzes combinations of items purchased together.
choices.DIVIDE with CALCULATE: Calculates the percentage of total sales contributed by each product.

correct_answer.RANKX: Ranks customers or products based on a measure.
correct_answer.CROSSJOIN: Analyzes combinations of items purchased together.
correct_answer.DIVIDE with CALCULATE: Calculates the percentage of total sales contributed by each product.

questions.explanation: These DAX patterns are essential for performing advanced sales and marketing analytics in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Describe how you would use the RANKX function in DAX to rank customers by their total purchases, and explain how this can help in targeting top customers.
questions.explanation: RANKX ranks customers based on their total purchases, allowing you to identify and target your top customers. For example, RANKX(ALL(Customers), SUM(Sales[Amount])) ranks customers by the sum of their purchases.

lessons.lesson_name: 5.3 DAX for Operational and HR Analytics

questions.question_text: You need to calculate the employee turnover rate for your company. Which of the following DAX formulas would you use?
questions.explanation: The turnover rate is calculated by dividing the number of terminated employees by the total number of employees, using CALCULATE to filter for terminated employees.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function AVERAGEX can be used to calculate the average tenure of employees within the company.
questions.explanation: AVERAGEX can be used to calculate the average tenure by evaluating the difference between hire date and termination date (or current date) for each employee.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ can be used to calculate the headcount of employees at the end of each month.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE combined with LASTDATE is often used to calculate the headcount by filtering the data to the last date of each month and counting active employees.

questions.question_text: Which DAX pattern would you use to calculate the number of hours worked by employees in a specific department over a given period?
questions.explanation: This pattern uses SUMX to sum the hours worked by employees, filtered by the specific department.

questions.question_text: True or False: The 'Cohort Analysis' DAX pattern is useful in HR analytics for analyzing the retention rate of employees hired in the same period.
questions.explanation: Cohort Analysis is a DAX pattern that groups employees by their hire date and tracks their retention over time, which is useful in HR analytics.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ is commonly used to calculate the total compensation for employees, including bonuses and benefits.
questions.explanation: SUMX is used to calculate total compensation by summing up the base salary, bonuses, and benefits for each employee.

questions.question_text: Match the following HR DAX patterns with their applications.

choices.Turnover Rate Calculation: Measures the rate at which employees leave the company.
choices.Headcount Calculation: Calculates the number of active employees at a specific point in time.

correct_answer.Turnover Rate Calculation: Measures the rate at which employees leave the company.
correct_answer.Headcount Calculation: Calculates the number of active employees at a specific point in time.

questions.explanation: These HR analytics patterns are essential for managing and analyzing employee data in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Describe how the 'Cohort Analysis' DAX pattern can be used to analyze employee retention, and provide an example of its application.
correct_answer: CALCULATE(COUNT(Employee[ID]), Employee[Hire Date] <= CohortDate, Employee[Termination Date] >= CohortDate)
questions.explanation: Cohort Analysis groups employees by hire date and tracks their retention over time. For example, CALCULATE(COUNT(Employee[ID]), Employee[Hire Date] <= CohortDate, Employee[Termination Date] >= CohortDate) calculates the number of employees retained in each cohort.

questions.question_text: For the capstone project, you are required to build a comprehensive Power BI report. Which of the following steps should you start with?
choices: Define the objectives and KPIs for the report
correct_answer: Define the objectives and KPIs for the report
questions.explanation: Defining the objectives and KPIs is the first step in creating a focused and effective report. This ensures that your visualizations and data analysis align with the business goals.

questions.question_text: True or False: For your capstone project, you should use real-time data sources whenever possible to ensure the report remains relevant.
questions.explanation: Using real-time data sources in Power BI ensures that your report is always up-to-date and relevant for decision-making.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: To maintain consistency in your report, it's important to establish a ______ before you start creating visualizations.
questions.explanation: A well-structured data model ensures consistency and accuracy in your analysis and visualizations.

questions.question_text: In the capstone project, how would you approach optimizing your DAX queries to improve report performance?
choices: Use variables to reduce redundant calculations
Avoid using measures and use calculated columns instead
Filter data with high cardinality columns
correct_answer: Use variables to reduce redundant calculations
questions.explanation: Using variables in your DAX queries helps optimize performance by reducing the need for redundant calculations.

questions.question_text: True or False: When designing the layout of your Power BI report, it's best to include as many visuals as possible on each page.
questions.explanation: Overloading a report page with visuals can make it difficult for users to focus on key insights. It's better to create a clean, focused layout.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: When dealing with a large dataset, it's important to use the ______ function in DAX to summarize data before aggregating.
questions.explanation: GROUPBY is used to summarize data, which is especially useful when working with large datasets to improve performance.

questions.question_text: Match the following key tasks in the capstone project with their correct descriptions.

choices.Define Objectives: Establishes the goals and KPIs for the report
choices.Optimize DAX: Improves query performance by using variables and efficient functions
choices.Design Layout: Ensures that the report is visually appealing and easy to navigate

questions.question_text: Which function assigns a unique sequential number to every row with no ties?
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique sequential values regardless of ties.

questions.question_text: RANK() is applied to salaries 9000, 8000, 8000, 7000. What rank does 7000 receive?
questions.explanation: Two rows share rank 2, so rank 3 is skipped and 7000 receives rank 4.

questions.question_text: Which clause inside OVER() restarts ranking per department?
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY resets the window function for each partition group.

questions.question_text: Which function looks at the PREVIOUS row's value within a window?
questions.explanation: LAG() retrieves a value from a prior row; LEAD() retrieves from a following row.

questions.question_text: LAST_VALUE() without a frame clause returns incorrect results because:
choices: It only looks up to the current row by default
correct_answer: It only looks up to the current row by default
questions.explanation: Default frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so LAST_VALUE sees only up to the current row.

questions.question_text: Fill the blank: SELECT Name, ___(Sales,1) OVER (ORDER BY Month) AS PrevSales FROM Sales
questions.explanation: LAG looks back one row; LEAD looks forward.

questions.question_text: DENSE_RANK() skips rank numbers after a tie.
questions.explanation: DENSE_RANK() never skips — that is RANK().

questions.question_text: NTILE(4) on 8 rows assigns bucket numbers:
questions.explanation: NTILE divides rows evenly across buckets in order.

questions.question_text: ROW_NUMBER() can produce the same value for two rows in the same partition.
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique values — ties are broken arbitrarily.

questions.question_text: To get the top earner per department you wrap a ROW_NUMBER() query and filter:
questions.explanation: Filtering rn=1 in the outer query returns one row per partition.

questions.question_text: FIRST_VALUE(Sales) OVER (PARTITION BY Dept ORDER BY Month) always returns:
choices: The first month's sales for that department
correct_answer: The first month's sales for that department
questions.explanation: FIRST_VALUE returns the first value in the ordered partition.

questions.question_text: The keyword that separates window functions into groups is ___.
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY resets the window per group.

questions.question_text: Which frame clause makes LAST_VALUE() return the true last value in a partition?
choices: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
correct_answer: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
questions.explanation: This extends the frame to cover all rows in the partition.

questions.question_text: LAG() returns NULL for the first row because there is no previous row.
questions.explanation: With no prior row, LAG returns NULL unless a default is specified.

questions.question_text: Sales growth = current month minus previous month. Which expression is correct?
questions.explanation: LAG gives the previous row's Sales; subtracting gives the growth.

questions.question_text: Which application do you open to write and run T-SQL window functions against SQL Server?
questions.explanation: SSMS is the primary IDE for SQL Server T-SQL development.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, where do you type your SQL query?
questions.explanation: The Query Editor is the central text area where you write T-SQL.

questions.question_text: What keyboard shortcut executes a query in SSMS?
questions.explanation: F5 (or clicking Execute) runs the selected or entire query in SSMS.

questions.question_text: How do you open a new query window in SSMS?
choices: File > New > Query with Current Connection
Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
correct_answer: Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
questions.explanation: Both methods open a fresh query editor tab connected to the current server.

questions.question_text: Where do you see query results after pressing F5 in SSMS?
choices: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
correct_answer: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
questions.explanation: Results appear in the bottom pane; the Messages tab shows row counts and errors.

questions.question_text: To switch to a different database inside SSMS, what are your two options?
choices: Only the database dropdown at the top toolbar
USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
correct_answer: USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
questions.explanation: Both methods work — the dropdown is quicker for ad hoc work.

questions.question_text: Where do you find existing stored procedures for a database in SSMS Object Explorer?
questions.explanation: Expand your database node, then Programmability, then Stored Procedures.

questions.question_text: How do you view and edit an existing stored procedure in SSMS?
choices: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
You must DROP and recreate it
correct_answer: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
questions.explanation: Right-click > Modify opens a query window pre-populated with ALTER PROCEDURE.

questions.question_text: How do you save a T-SQL script in SSMS?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S saves your query to a local .sql file you can reopen later.

questions.question_text: How do you call (execute) a stored procedure with parameters in T-SQL?
questions.explanation: EXEC (or EXECUTE) followed by the procedure name and named parameters is the correct syntax.

questions.question_text: To see the actual execution plan for a query in SSMS, what do you do?
choices: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
Open a new window and type EXPLAIN
correct_answer: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
questions.explanation: Ctrl+M toggles 'Include Actual Execution Plan' — the plan tab appears after you run the query.

questions.question_text: After writing a CREATE PROCEDURE statement in SSMS, what must you do to save it to the database?
choices: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
Both Ctrl+S and F5 are required
correct_answer: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
questions.explanation: Running CREATE PROCEDURE registers it in the database. Ctrl+S only saves the script file locally.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, pressing F5 with text selected will execute only the selected text, not the entire script.
questions.explanation: If you highlight a portion of the query before pressing F5, only that portion runs.

questions.question_text: You can only have one Query Editor tab open at a time in SSMS.
questions.explanation: SSMS supports multiple tabbed Query Editor windows simultaneously.

lessons.lesson_name: Module 2 – CTE, Temp Tables & Table Variables

questions.question_text: What keyword starts a CTE?
questions.explanation: CTEs begin with the WITH keyword followed by the CTE name.

questions.question_text: A recursive CTE must contain:
choices: An anchor member UNION ALL a recursive member
Two SELECT statements joined by UNION
correct_answer: An anchor member UNION ALL a recursive member
questions.explanation: The anchor provides the starting rows; the recursive part joins back to the CTE.

questions.question_text: Which temp table type is visible to ALL active sessions?
questions.explanation: ## prefix makes the table visible across all sessions.

questions.question_text: A @TableVariable does NOT support:
questions.explanation: Table variables have no statistics, leading to poor cardinality estimates on large sets.

questions.question_text: When does a #Temp table get automatically dropped?
questions.explanation: #Temp tables persist for the entire session and are dropped when the connection closes.

questions.question_text: A CTE can be referenced multiple times in the same query.
questions.explanation: Unlike a subquery, a CTE can be referenced more than once in the query that defines it.

questions.question_text: Fill: WITH ___ AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM ___
questions.explanation: The CTE name is used both in the definition and the reference.

questions.question_text: A @TableVariable rolls back when a ROLLBACK TRANSACTION is issued.
questions.explanation: Table variable changes survive a ROLLBACK — useful for error logging.

questions.question_text: Which is best for large intermediate datasets that need an index?
